artboards.title: C · Market floor — submit a job

annotations.text:
THE QUESTION
Would a stranger believe this is a first-tier product in the first five seconds?

Scored against linear.app, vercel.com, stripe.com, railway.com, fly.io and the Hypervisor shell.

All three directions use the SAME identity: the owner's reserved mark, and the adopted drawn Z and I (the brand face's own Z reads as a 2 and its I as a 1 — three readers typed digits for both).

Every colour is a token from the design system. Every number is read off the live daemon.

A · LEDGER
Axis: evidence as the aesthetic.

Archivo + IBM Plex Mono. Hairline rules do the work colour usually does. Green reserved strictly for live evidence. One filled button per screen.

Tradeoff: it is quiet. Reads as serious; could read as plain.

B · INSTRUMENT PANEL
Axis: inverted and instrumented.

Space Grotesk + JetBrains Mono on onyx. Green lifted to the on-dark token. Reads as a live instrument, not a document.

Tradeoff: dark flatters screenshots and punishes long reading — and this product depends on honesty copy people actually read.

C · MARKET FLOOR
Axis: editorial and argued.

Newsreader for argument, Archivo for data, Plex Mono for evidence. Warm paper, asymmetric grid, one funnel diagram carrying the product's actual idea.

Tradeoff: the most opinionated, the least console-like. Risks reading as marketing attached to a tool.
